claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation.

Let me begin with a basic question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have one child I'd like to ask about - my son Alex. He's 13.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'll be assessing eligibility for your son Alex, who is 13.

Let me start by asking some questions to understand your family situation better.

**First, does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the situation better.

**Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. That's helpful context.

**Are you currently paying child maintenance or child support to Alex's mum for his care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute towards his upkeep - I help with things like his clothes, school expenses, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to understand the specific arrangements a bit better.

**Is the money you contribute given directly to Alex's mum as formal child maintenance payments, or are you purchasing items like clothes and school expenses directly for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I give the money directly to his mum to help with his costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I have a good understanding of your situation now, but let me just confirm one more important detail.

**Are you a British citizen or do you have settled status in the UK? Also, do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important information. Before I provide my assessment, let me read the specific eligibility rules to ensure I give you accurate guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment.

However, I need to clarify one final point to complete my evaluation:

**You mentioned you're living abroad - are you a UK citizen or Crown servant, or do you have any specific status that would allow you to claim Child Benefit while living outside the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm just living abroad - I don't have any special status like being a Crown servant or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on all the information you've provided, I now have enough to make my assessment.

## Summary

I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit at this time.

While you do meet one of the responsibility criteria by making regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (clothes, school expenses, etc.), the fundamental requirement for Child Benefit is that you must live in the UK. 

The rules allow for some exceptions for people living abroad (such as Crown servants or those living in certain specific countries), but as you're living abroad without any of these qualifying statuses, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you move back to the UK—you would then be able to reassess your eligibility. If you have any questions or your situation changes, you can always contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
